items.title: Trump Suggests Ukraine Needs a New President, Blasting Zelenskyy
items.author: Catherine Lucey
items.content: <article>President Donald Trump demanded that Volodymyr Zelenskyy halt attacks on Russian oil refineries and suggested he should consider stepping aside as Ukraine’s president, escalating a fight centered on securing more diesel supplies for the US ahead of the midterm elections.</article>

items.title: Saudi Arabia Suspends Riyadh Airport Operations After Attack
items.author: Sara Gharaibeh and Kateryna Kadabashy
items.content: <article>Saudi Arabia said it temporarily suspended operations at the Riyadh airport Saturday after an “enemy” attack as air traffic was disrupted for the third time this week amid an intensifying conflict with Yemen’s Houthis.</article>

items.title: Trump Turns to Russia as Diesel Prices Rise
items.content: <article>Bloomberg Congressional Reporter Caitlin Reilly and ABC News State Department Reporter Shannon Kingston join hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini on Bloomberg This Weekend to discuss President Donald Trump's agreement to obtain Russian diesel as rising energy costs put pressure on Republicans ahead of the midterm elections. They examine Ukraine's objections to the deal, disagreements over tariffs and the Iran war in competitive Senate races, and Secretary of State Marco Rubio's foreign policy agenda amid allegations involving the US ambassador to Greece. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Supreme Court Recusals in Spotlight as Alito Drops From Oil Case
items.author: Greg Stohr
items.content: <article>Justice Samuel Alito’s decision not to take part in a major climate-change case because of his wife’s stock holdings is putting renewed focus on the US Supreme Court’s recusal practices as it kicks off its new nine-month term.</article>

items.title: Trump Hypes Megaprojects to Voters Who Lament Gas, Food Costs
items.author: Jennifer A. Dlouhy and Josh Wingrove
items.content: <article>Presidents have long made bombastic pledges to voters in last-minute electoral appeals.</article>

items.title: Cockroach Party Leaders Detained to Stop Protests
items.content: <article>Indian authorities detained Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke and spokespersons Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka ahead of a planned demonstration against a contentious revision of voter rolls. Police imposed sweeping restrictions in the national capital to stop supporters and allies from gathering for the youth-led protest. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: EU Plans Measures to Halve Imports of Chinese Hybrid Cars
items.author: Donato Paolo Mancini, Jenny Leonard and Alberto Nardelli
items.content: <article>The European Union intends to use safeguard measures to cut the number of hybrid car imports from China by half, according to people familiar with the discussions.</article>

items.title: EU Eyes €160 Billion Cut to Proposed Budget Heading to Talks
items.author: Suzanne Lynch
items.content: <article>European Union leaders will discuss a scaled back budget when they meet in Brussels next week after negotiators slashed the initial proposal in response to pressure from some countries.</article>

items.title: Burnham’s Senior Officials Are Trading Blame Over Economic Pain
items.author: Alex Wickham
items.content: <article>Andy Burnham ended a barnstorming speech at his party conference last week by pledging to restore a spirit of unity to the country. By the time he walked off stage he seemed to have succeeded in something much harder: restoring unity to his own party.</article>

items.title: India Police Detain Protesters, Lock Down Delhi Over Voter Rolls
items.author: Rajesh Roy, Atul Dev and Asmi Bhatia
items.content: <article>Police in India’s capital cracked down on protests against a contentious review of voter rolls, detaining youth leaders and locking down central New Delhi with thousands of security personnel.</article>

items.title: Trump Warns Norway He Won’t Forget Nobel Peace Prize Snub
items.author: Jennifer A. Dlouhy and Catherine Lucey
items.content: <article>President Donald Trump fumed at the Norwegian committee that awards the Nobel Peace Prize, saying that the fact it didn’t go to him “is just another sign of how Norway and all these others are ripping off our country.”</article>

items.title: Charlamagne Tha God on Netflix Deal, Midterm Elections, Mental Health
items.content: <article>Charlamagne Tha God joins Bloomberg's Romaine Bostick to talk about the world of podcasting, the "Breakfast Club" partnership on Netflix, midterm elections and much more. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Trump: Putin To Release Diesel Into Global Market
items.content: <article>"Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Rep. Debbie Wasserman Schultz (D-FL) says President Trump’s deal with Russia to release diesel supplies is a “desperate political move” designed to help Republicans ahead of the midterms and argues he cares more about his party’s political outcome than addressing the cost of living. Robert Post, professor and former dean at Yale Law School, says allowing the Trump administration to decide which members of the press can access the White House could “deform the press coverage of the president” and leave the public without complete coverage. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Bessent Will Likely Cut US Long Bond Sales Next Month, Says Citi
items.author: Greg Ritchie
items.content: <article>US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is likely to reduce the auction sizes for long-dated government bonds — and could even cancel sales of 20-year debt altogether, according to Citigroup Inc.</article>

items.title: DOJ Scrutinizes Binance Compliance With 2023 Settlement Deal
items.author: Chris Strohm
items.content: <article>The US Justice Department is scrutinizing whether Binance Holdings Ltd. breached a landmark settlement with the US government, as authorities probe activity on the platform for potential Iran sanctions violations.</article>

items.title: Post Says White House Press Limits Could ‘Deform’ Coverage
items.content: <article>Robert Post, professor and former dean at Yale Law School, says allowing the Trump administration to decide which members of the press can access the White House could “deform the press coverage of the president” and leave the public without complete coverage. Post says the broader conflict between the administration and the courts is a difficult one because courts rely on the executive branch’s good-faith compliance to enforce their orders. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Trump Says Putin to Supply US With Diesel Ahead of Midterms
items.author: Catherine Lucey, Jennifer A. Dlouhy and Will Kubzansky
items.content: <article>President Donald Trump is working with Vladimir Putin to release Russian diesel supplies into global markets, a move that upends years of sanctions as the White House seeks ways to tame soaring fuel prices ahead of the US midterm election.</article>

items.title: EU Says China Will Cut Hybrid Car Exports by Millions
items.author: Linda Lew and Jorge Valero
items.content: <article>The European Union said China agreed to slash millions of hybrid car exports to the bloc, pointing to a potential trade detente before EU leaders meet next week to discuss further steps against Beijing.</article>

items.title: India Slams Vance for ‘Offensive’ Remarks on Foreign Workers
items.author: Sudhi Ranjan Sen
items.content: <article>India’s government criticized Vice President JD Vance for “deeply offensive” remarks in which he referred to foreign recruits at software firms in the US, many of whom are Indians, as servants.</article>

items.title: New Delhi Deploys Heavy Security Ahead of Voter-Roll Protest
items.author: Rajesh Roy and Sudhi Ranjan Sen
items.content: <article>From mass detentions to liquor-store closures, authorities in New Delhi are leaving little to chance as they prepare for a weekend of protests over a contentious revision of India’s voter rolls.</article>
